### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/spec`, touching **6** documentable anchor(s).

**4** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/automation/flows.mdx`  _(via addDays (literal, a string literal in NOW_ANCHOR_KEYS))_
- `content/docs/data-modeling/fields.mdx`  _(via addDays (literal, a string literal in NOW_ANCHOR_KEYS))_
- `content/docs/data-modeling/formulas.mdx`  _(via addDays (literal, a string literal in NOW_ANCHOR_KEYS))_
- `content/docs/protocol/objectql/query-syntax.mdx`  _(via addDays (literal, a string literal in NOW_ANCHOR_KEYS))_

⛔ **2** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v16.mdx`  _(via addDays (literal, a string literal in NOW_ANCHOR_KEYS))_
- `content/docs/releases/v18/18-2.mdx`  _(via addDays (literal, a string literal in NOW_ANCHOR_KEYS))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **55** of **207** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **147** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 68edbcf10fdc8351d6238c6a9a34e0cc66c71bb0` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `4245e590d1b9132fbbf868f5cc8798b51c08f93c` — the merge of head `98b536ffd50ac587f83c82e55b5aadaa5db73118` into base `68edbcf10fdc8351d6238c6a9a34e0cc66c71bb0`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 4245e590d1b9132fbbf868f5cc8798b51c08f93c && git checkout 4245e590d1b9132fbbf868f5cc8798b51c08f93c
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 68edbcf10fdc8351d6238c6a9a34e0cc66c71bb0 98b536ffd50ac587f83c82e55b5aadaa5db73118 && git checkout -B drift-repro 68edbcf10fdc8351d6238c6a9a34e0cc66c71bb0 && git merge --no-ff 98b536ffd50ac587f83c82e55b5aadaa5db73118

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 68edbcf10fdc8351d6238c6a9a34e0cc66c71bb0
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 68edbcf10fdc8351d6238c6a9a34e0cc66c71bb0` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `98b536ffd50ac587f83c82e55b5aadaa5db73118`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/data/filter-comparand-type.ts + packages/spec/src/data/filter.zod.ts (NowAnchorSchema, the FilterConditionSchema save door at parseFilterAST), packages/objectql/src/engine.ts (lowerWhereFilterArray, the aggregations[i].filter and having doors), packages/objectql/src/having-filter.ts, packages/core/src/utils/filter-tokens.ts (resolveNowAnchor), packages/drivers/driver-sql/src/sql-driver.ts (nowAnchorOf), packages/formula/src/matches-filter.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/rls-compiler.ts (judgeCompiledComparands), packages/spec/src/shared/strict-object.ts (closedObject), skills/objectstack-query/rules/filters.md

Inputs read: card #26413 (body and all six comments, the two os-dev reports and the withdrawal note included), PR #26592 (body, file list, net diff against main at this head), and the check-runs on the head. The rest of the diff (the changeset and the three test files outside spec) is the lane seat's ACCEPT at TIER_DEFAULT.

Check-runs at the time of this record: every required job is completed and green, including Lint and Repo Gates, TypeScript Type Check, Check Changeset, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Spec property liveness, Dogfood Regression Gate, Build Core and all eight Test Core shards. Test Core (5/8) was still in progress on my first read and finished green before this record was closed. The skipped jobs are the UI, docs, temporal and opt-in lanes that this diff does not reach.

### ① Derived judgments

1. Accept-set change at the comparand-type walk. `isWellFormedNowAnchor` now answers false for any key other than `$now` and `addDays`, and `malformedNowAnchorRefusal` gains a first arm that names every undeclared key. Read in the live tree, this is one function on one walk, and the walk is the one every platform filter door runs. Right.

2. Which doors this reaches. I traced each one in the cited code. `lowerWhereFilterArray` in engine.ts runs `normalizeFilterComparandTypes` on the object form and `parseFilterAST` on the array form, and it is called by find, findOne, update, delete, count and aggregate. The aggregations[i].filter door runs the walk at engine.ts near line 20456 and the having door at line 20539. `parseFilterAST` in filter.zod.ts runs the walk on everything it returns, and the FilterConditionSchema save door goes through it. The RLS compiler's `judgeCompiledComparands` also runs the walk, for `using` and `check` alike. So the PR's door list is right, and it is in fact one door short in its own favour: the RLS compile seam refuses the same anchor too. The changeset's "every filter door" claim holds.

3. The door runs before the resolver. `lowerWhereFilterArray` runs ahead of `resolveWhereFilterTokens`, and `resolveNowAnchor` in filter-tokens.ts spreads the node unchanged apart from pinning `$now`. So the authored form is judged, and the resolved form the engine hands the executors carries no system-added key that the walk could trip on. The test for the resolved form (`$now` holding an ISO string plus `note`) pins the same refusal. Right.

4. Executors are unchanged and consistent. `nowAnchorOf` in driver-sql, `resolveNowAnchor` in core, having-filter.ts and the formula evaluator all read `$now` and `addDays` by shape and nothing else. None of them needs a change, because no extra key reaches them through a door any more. Right.

5. The formula evaluator's tolerance stays, scoped. `matchesFilterCondition` called directly still reads an anchor by shape. Every in-repo caller sits behind a door that runs the walk: having-filter.ts (having and the per-aggregation fallback), and plugin-security's write check, whose parts come out of `judgeCompiledComparands`. The explain engine and the tenant wall hand it engine-built filters that carry no anchor. The retitled test says exactly this. Right, and the card's "retire or narrow" wording allows it.

6. Public surface. `NOW_ANCHOR_KEYS` and `undeclaredNowAnchorKeys` are module-private. No export, type or error code is added or renamed. The refusal reuses `INVALID_FILTER` / 400. No generated spec artifact moves. Right.

7. The restated key set. `NOW_ANCHOR_KEYS` is a local copy of NowAnchorSchema's two keys, because filter.zod.ts imports this module and the reverse import would be a cycle. The reconciliation test reads `NowAnchorSchema.shape`. I checked that `closedObject` builds a ZodObject subclass from the same def and that `lazySchema` proxies property reads to the real instance, so `.shape` is live. The drift guard is real. Right.

8. The skill sentence. skills/objectstack-query/rules/filters.md line 78 already says any extra key is refused with `INVALID_FILTER` / 400, and the eval forbids `subDays`. This diff makes the sentence true. `Skills-docs: none` is right. The Docs Drift advisory lists four hand-written pages that name `addDays`; I read query-syntax.mdx and it says there is no `subDays`, which agrees with the new refusal. Nothing to edit.

### ② Semver level

`@objectstack/spec: minor`. Right.

- `Metadata-protocol: narrowed` is measured, not asserted: FilterConditionSchema accepted `{ $now: true, addDays: -30, subDays: 7 }` on base and refuses it now, and a filter is something a metadata author writes (views, datasets, policies). AGENTS.md Post-Task Checklist step 3 makes a declared kind at least `minor` on the package the diff moves. The dispatch said `patch`, and the dev was right to deviate and said so in the report. The dispatch's `Metadata-protocol: as measured by the dev` left the kind to the measurement.
- `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` matches the diff: nothing widens, and an input that ran now refuses. The triage comment's `yes (narrowing)` was the earlier reading; the question the line answers is whether the card widens the accept set or the public surface, and the answer is no. The PR body and the changeset carry the same line, byte for byte on the value and the arm.
- BREAKING banner, `fix(spec)!:` title and one ADR-0087 marker, `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`, are present in the changeset body. The disposition is sound: no key is added, removed or renamed, an extra key had no meaning at any executor, so there is no FROM to TO rewrite. `check-adr-0087-registration` and Check Changeset are green on the head.
- objectql and formula change tests only and publish nothing. No changeset owed.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Report 6436343165 (needs_decision, option A or B). Answered by the re-laning note 6436359662 and the spec-seat claim 6437371136: option A, the shared walk. This PR is option A. Closed.
- The dev's deviation from `patch` to `minor`. Answered in ② above: the rule in AGENTS.md decides, and the dev followed it. Closed.
- The formula pin, "narrowed, not retired". Answered in ① item 5: every in-repo caller sits behind a door that runs the walk. Closed.
- Out-of-scope note, carried from the earlier report: the bare implicit-equality spelling `{ opened_at: { $now: true, addDays: -30, note: 'x' } }` is read by the walk as an operator bag and is not judged here. Read in the cited code, it is not a silent run either: the `$now` key reaches the drivers as an operator name, and driver-sql's `nowAnchorPositionError` and having-filter.ts line 1780 refuse it. Its answer on driver-memory is not measured. A note in the acceptance notes is the right carrier under Prime Directive 10; a card is owed only if someone measures a silent answer. Not escalated.
- `open_questions` on the final report: empty. Nothing left to escalate.

### ④ Design judgment

packages/spec/src/data/filter-comparand-type.ts

The change holds against the code it cites and the scenario it is accepted against: an author writes `subDays: 7` on a now-anchor, and every door answers one `INVALID_FILTER` / 400 that names the key. I tried to break it along these lines.

- Order of the arms. Undeclared keys are checked before the `addDays` arm, in both the predicate and the refusal, so `{ $now: true, subDays: 7 }` is told about `subDays` first, which is the key the author got wrong. The refusal lists every undeclared key, not just the first. Good.
- Guard agreement. `isNowAnchor` admits an object whose `$now` is `true` or a string, which is exactly the shape driver-sql's `nowAnchorOf` reads, so a refusal here is never for a shape an executor would have accepted. The predicate and the refusal read one helper, `undeclaredNowAnchorKeys`, so they cannot disagree on the set.
- Keys with an undefined value. `Object.keys` counts `{ note: undefined }`, so it is refused with `note` named while the JSON preview omits it. Zod's strict object refuses the same key, so the walk agrees with the declaration. Not reachable from JSON. Not a finding.
- Copy-on-write contract. The anchor branch answers keep or refuse and never narrows, so a well-formed anchor still returns the same reference; the new test pins it.
- Cycle and drift. The local key set is the price of filter.zod.ts importing this module, and the shape reconciliation test is the drift guard. The comment says why. Good.
- Refusal length. The canonical sentence with the engine prefix, `find('ticket'): ... subDays ...`, is 496 characters, four under the 500-character client bound the module header cites. A longer field name, a path under `$and`, or a second undeclared key pushes it over, and the client then drops the tail, which is the "NOT applied" sentence. The load-bearing parts (path, preview, key names, the two-key rule) are front-loaded, so the author still gets the key, and the sibling arms sit at a similar length. The fixed clause "(there is no subDays: a negative addDays subtracts)" costs 52 characters and is printed even when the only extra key is `note`. should-fix: make that clause conditional on `subDays` being among the keys, or shorten it, so the common one-key case stays inside the bound with the "NOT applied" sentence intact. Not a must-fix: no door answers wrong rows, and the refusal still names the key.
- Stale sentence. The `isNowAnchor` docblock still says a malformed anchor is refused by its own schema sentence and by each executor; the next docblock says the walk refuses it HERE. The second is the one that is true for every door. should-fix: trim the first to match, on the next touch.

No must-fix found. The tree does what the card's option (a) asked for and what the skill already taught.

Implemented-by: `claude/project-thread-34f9ql`
Reviewed-by: `session_01WGufzfhobWEgUUrjz4rrbh`

**VERDICT: PASS**

## 席位核对 · ACCEPT · `domain:spec` seat 1 (#6017) · session `session_01WGufzfhobWEgUUrjz4rrbh` · 2026-10-27T09:54Z

Head `98b536ffd50ac587f83c82e55b5aadaa5db73118`. Card #26413 (option (a), triage `6433326089`), claim `6437371136` amended by `6438758345`, dev report `6438607776`.

- **Contract review:** owed at CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER for two reasons. `packages/spec/src/data/filter-comparand-type.ts` is touched, and the card is a narrowing. PASS `6438749334` names this head. The shared comparand walk now refuses any `$now` anchor key beyond `$now` / `addDays`, and names the extra key first. The reviewer traced it through every door: find, findOne, update, delete, count, aggregate, `aggregations[i].filter`, `having`, the `FilterConditionSchema` save door and the RLS compile seam. The walk judges the authored form before the token resolver runs. No export or error code moves. The formula evaluator's by-shape read stays only behind those doors, and its pin is narrowed, not retired.
- **Two should-fixes, not carried:** (1) the one-key refusal is 496 characters, close to the 500-character client bound. The fixed "there is no subDays" clause prints even when the key is `note`, so a long path can cut off the "NOT applied" tail, but the key is still named first. (2) The `isNowAnchor` docblock has one stale sentence. Both are below the filing bar. Take them on the next touch of this file.
- **Deviation from the order, accepted:** the order said `patch`. The dev measured the save door narrowing, so `Metadata-protocol: narrowed` and `'@objectstack/spec': minor` per AGENTS.md step 3. The claim is amended to match. There is a BREAKING banner and one ADR-0087 marker (`not-required (no-migration-prescription)`), and there is no key to rewrite.
- **Shape:** `Fixes #26413`, 6 files. `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` and `Metadata-protocol: narrowed` on the body, the changeset and the amended claim. `Skills-docs: none`, because `filters.md` already taught the refusal and now it is true. `check-governed-merges --pr 26592`: NOT governed, 196 changed lines.
- **Gates:** check-runs on the head are 40 success, 8 skipped and 0 red. `mergeable_state` is clean.
- **Landing:** Tier S. `pr_ready` + `automerge_enable` in this act.
